# Feature: Lava tile — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #44 (Lava tile) from Terrain and Hazards before it is used in real levels. Effect: Static lethal lava that never spreads and destroys ice blocks. Unique: static lethal lava, permanent and uncancellable. Useful: the hazard you must route around or fill, never put out. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** static lethal lava that never spreads and destroys ice blocks.

**So that** the hazard you must route around or fill, never put out.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Lava tile for the first time in its teaching room (mech-44-lava-tile-room). Teaching moment: First room: a lava tile with an ice block beside it, placed after the player has learned that ice cancels fire. A player who pushes the block into the lava watches it melt while the lava remains and must restart the room, which teaches that lava is not a stronger fire and cannot be cancelled at all. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: A fixed lava tile, lethal to step on, that never spreads or burns out
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: An ice block pushed into it melts and is destroyed and the lava stays
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Nothing cancels lava
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: You route around it or fill it with dirt

## Edge Cases & Rules

- A fixed lava tile, lethal to step on, that never spreads or burns out
- An ice block pushed into it melts and is destroyed and the lava stays
- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.
- No soft-lock: every reachable state has a legal move, a lose, or a reset.
- Definition audit: lava: fixed hazard defined here; entering it loses the attempt, it never spreads or burns out and nothing cancels it
- Definition audit: fire: cancellable, burning-out hazard per mechanic 43 in this file; lava is explicitly not a stronger fire
- Definition audit: ice block: per mechanic 82 in blocks.yml; in lava it melts and is destroyed while the lava stays
- Definition audit: dirt block: the one block that fills lava into floor, per mechanic 90 in blocks.yml

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Lava tile's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Testing

Needs a mechanics playground: new — Test Level mech-44-lava-tile-room, built from this mechanic's teaching moment above. What to check there: every rule in Player-Facing Behavior, played in mech-44-lava-tile-room; the teaching moment's first (naive) action should fail as described and the corrected action should succeed. Record play sessions for replay: yes — sessions are the review evidence. Synergy rooms are explicitly deferred to a later run and are not part of this feature's check.
Named test cases (from the candidate file; all must be played):
- Test case lethal and permanent: stepping on lava loses the attempt (or returns to the active checkpoint), and the lava tile is unchanged afterwards
- Test case ice does not cancel lava: blocked-by: 82 (ice block): pushing an ice block in melts the block and the lava stays, unlike fire
- Test case adversarial route-around: every lava tile in the room can be routed around or filled; no route requires standing on lava or leaves the player stranded
- Test case restart and replay: restart restores the room, and a recorded session replays to the same end state
